h1:
Things to Do in Krabi
16 Spots Worth Your Time
intro: Krabi is one of those places where you can switch up the whole vibe in a single day. Hop on a boat in the morning for the 4 Islands tour and walk across the separated sea, drive inland in the afternoon to soak in a hot-spring waterfall and then dip in the Emerald Pool, and finish the day watching the sunset at Railay Beach. We've picked 16 spots that real travelers actually visit and that are worth your time — split into beaches, islands, inland nature, and culture — with entry fees and opening hours checked fresh for 2026.

blocks.html: Krabi is different from Phuket in that the highlights are spread across several zones. The beaches and tour piers sit down south around Ao Nang, while the inland nature — the Emerald Pool, the hot spring, Tiger Cave Temple — is tucked further in toward Khlong Thom district and Krabi town, about a 40-minute to one-hour drive from Ao Nang. The trick to not wearing yourself out is to do one theme per day: a boat day for the islands, a land day for the nature. It's far easier than zigzagging back and forth.

Krabi's beaches stand out for the towering limestone cliffs rising straight out of the sea — nothing like a wide-open beach elsewhere. Ao Nang is the hub for hotels and restaurants, while Railay and Phra Nang Bay take a short longtail-boat ride more but are well worth it. The clear-water, calm-sea season runs from November to April. In the rainy season (May–Oct) the swell picks up and some boat trips get cancelled, so always check the flags and listen to the boatmen before getting in the water.

items.name: Ao Nang
items.blurb: The hub of any Krabi trip. A long stretch of beach lined with seafront restaurants, cafes, and an evening walking street. Free to enter, and it's the departure point for nearly every boat to Railay and the island tours. It makes a great base since onward travel is easy and there's plenty to eat.

items.name: Railay Beach + Phra Nang Bay
items.blurb: White-sand beaches ringed by limestone cliffs — this is a magnet for rock climbers from all over the world. You can't reach it by road; you take a longtail boat from Ao Nang, about 10–15 minutes (roughly 100–150 THB per person). Phra Nang Bay has Phra Nang Cave and clearer water, and it's great for sunset.

items.name: Talay Waek (the Separated Sea)
items.blurb: The highlight of the 4 Islands tour — a sandbar linking Koh Kai, Koh Tap, and Koh Mor that surfaces at low tide so you can walk across. It only appears at low tide, so check the tide schedule with your tour first. It's part of the 4 Islands tour, not a separate trip.

items.name: Koh Poda
items.blurb: A white-sand, clear-water island on the 4 Islands circuit, with a gorgeous limestone karst as a backdrop. Great for swimming and photos. It's already included in the 4 Islands tour, with a separate national-park fee on top of the tour price.

blocks.title: Beach tips
blocks.html: Longtail boats to Railay have a public shared-boat queue at Ao Nang — the fare is charged per head and the boat leaves once it's full. If you don't want to wait, you can charter a whole boat, but it costs more. Agree on the return fare clearly before you set off, because in the late afternoon there are fewer boats and prices creep up.

blocks.title: Want more out of Krabi? Book tours & activities
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.html: The real magic of Krabi is getting on a boat and heading out to the islands. Most tours leave from Ao Nang pier or Nopparat Thara pier, with a choice of local-feel longtail boats or speedboats that save time. In high season (Nov–Apr), book about a week ahead and budget extra for the national-park fees (Thai nationals pay far less than foreigners).

items.name: 4 Islands Tour
items.blurb: Krabi's classic trip, covering Talay Waek, Koh Kai, Koh Poda, and Phra Nang Cave at Railay. A longtail boat runs about 900–1,200 THB per person; speedboats are faster and cost more. There's a national-park fee of around 200 THB per person on top. Great for a first visit.

items.name: Hong Islands
items.blurb: An island group in Than Bok Khorani National Park, known for the emerald-green inner lagoon ringed by cliffs and a 360-degree viewpoint. Longtail-boat tours start around 900 THB and speedboats around 1,100 THB per person. Quieter and prettier water than the 4 Islands, with a park fee on top.

items.name: Phi Phi Islands + Maya Bay
items.blurb: The islands made famous by the film The Beach — cliffs and emerald-green water. A one-day speedboat tour from Krabi runs about 1,490–1,590 THB per person, covering Maya Bay, Pileh Lagoon, and snorkeling stops. The boat ride takes around 45 minutes. You can visit Maya Bay, but there are rules limiting going in the water.

items.name: Koh Lanta
items.blurb: A large island in southern Krabi with a slower pace than Ao Nang — long, quiet beaches, the Lanta Old Town, and the lighthouse at Mu Ko Lanta National Park. Ideal if you want to settle in for several nights and escape the bustle. You get there by car and then a ferry from Krabi town.

blocks.title: Island tips
blocks.html: You can only walk across Talay Waek at low tide. A good tour will time things to hit low tide just right; if you're booking on your own, ask the company what time low tide falls that day. On some days the water doesn't drop enough and you'll only see a thin sandbar. And remember that the national-park fee is different for Thais and foreigners, so bring cash.

Krabi isn't just the sea. Deep in the forest around Khlong Thom there are natural hot springs and emerald-colored pools that are hard to find anywhere else. Most people make a one-day trip combining the hot-spring waterfall, the Emerald Pool, and Tiger Cave Temple, since they're all fairly close together. You can drive yourself or buy a tour either way. Bring shoes that handle slippery ground.

items.name: Emerald Pool
items.blurb: A natural emerald-green pool in the forest of the Khao Pra-Bang Khram Wildlife Sanctuary. You can wade in for a swim, then walk on to the Blue Pool nearby. Open roughly 8:30–16:30, entry around 40 THB for Thais (20 for kids) and around 200 THB for foreigners. A great way to cool off.

items.name: Hot Spring Waterfall
items.blurb: Natural hot mineral water flowing down in tiers of smooth limestone basins, around 40–50°C — you can soak away the aches like an onsen. It's near the Emerald Pool, so people pair the two in one day. Entry runs around 90–200 THB depending on nationality. Go in the morning for smaller crowds.

items.name: Tiger Cave Temple
items.blurb: A forest-monastery temple with a natural cave and 1,237 steps up to a chedi at the summit, with a 360-degree view over the whole province. The temple grounds are free; climbing to the top costs around 50 THB. Open roughly 6:30–17:00. Go early morning or late afternoon to dodge the heat, and bring enough water.

items.name: Than Bok Khorani
items.blurb: A clear-water park set in the forest of Ao Luek district — green pools under big shade trees where you can swim and walk forest trails. The atmosphere is shady and there are fewer people than at the Emerald Pool. Cheap to enter, and great if you want quiet nature on the way to Ao Luek.

blocks.title: Nature tips
blocks.html: The Emerald Pool and the Hot Spring Waterfall sit along the same route near Khlong Thom, so you can easily do both in one trip — but it's about an hour from Ao Nang. If you're not driving yourself, a one-day tour with transfers included works out better. The 1,237 steps at Tiger Cave Temple really are steep and hot, so if your heart isn't up for it, you can just look around the temple grounds at the bottom instead.

Krabi town is small but full of charm. Along the Krabi River, two limestone karsts flank the water as the symbol of the province. You can stroll the evening market, see the black-crab sculpture in the middle of town, and take a boat to see the caves — all in half a day. It makes a nice easy day before or after you tackle the sea and the forest.

items.name: Khao Khanab Nam
items.blurb: Two limestone karsts flanking the Krabi River, the symbol of the province. Take a longtail (hua thong) boat from Chao Fa Pier, about 15 minutes (around 170 THB per person, or 500–800 THB to charter a boat). You can climb up to see the stalactite-and-stalagmite cave for around 30 THB; ancient human skeletons were once excavated here.

items.name: Krabi Town + Evening Market
items.blurb: An easygoing riverside town with the black-crab sculpture in the center, a bridge across the river, and the Krabi walking street on weekends with southern street food and craft stalls. Free to enter, and great for soaking up the local atmosphere and finding dinner.

items.name: Shell Cemetery (75 Million Years Old)
items.blurb: A field of rock formed from layer upon layer of compacted shells, tens of millions of years old, along the sea at Ban Laem Pho. It's one of only a handful of fossil sites like it in the world. Free to enter and quick to walk through — a good stop along the way for anyone into geology and the unusual.

items.name: Wat Maha That Wachira Mongkol (Wat Bang Thong)
items.blurb: A temple in Ao Luek district with a large, gleaming golden chedi — photogenic and peaceful. Free to enter; dress modestly. Fewer crowds than Tiger Cave Temple, so it's good for the spiritually inclined or anyone wanting to stop at a beautiful temple on the way to Ao Luek.

blocks.text: How to Plan Your Days Without Burning Out

blocks.html: Krabi is most fun when you do one theme per day, since the sea and the inland nature are in opposite directions. Here's a sample 3-day plan that actually flows, using Ao Nang as your base.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Islands: 4 Islands tour & the separated sea

items.activity: Tour pickup at your hotel, board the boat at Ao Nang pier
Walk Talay Waek at low tide, swim at Koh Poda
items.note: Check the tide schedule with your tour

items.activity: Lunch on the island, then snorkeling
Back at Ao Nang, stroll the evening walking street

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Nature: forest, hot spring & Emerald Pool

items.activity: Leave Ao Nang for Khlong Thom
items.note: Drive yourself or take a one-day tour

items.activity: Soak in the hot-spring waterfall, then walk down to the Emerald Pool
Climb Tiger Cave Temple — 1,237 steps for the view
items.note: Go late afternoon to dodge the heat

items.activity: Longtail boat to Railay Beach & Phra Nang Bay
Back to Ao Nang, rest through the hottest part of the day
Head into Krabi town, take a boat to see Khao Khanab Nam
Walk the Krabi evening market, find southern food
items.note: An easy way to wrap up the trip

items: Car / motorbike rental — the most convenient option, since the inland nature is spread far apart. A rental car runs about 1,000–1,500 THB/day, a motorbike about 250–350 THB/day. You'll need a license and a helmet.
Ride apps (Grab/Bolt) — available in Ao Nang and town, but with fewer cars than Phuket. Late at night or outside town you may wait a while. Prices are set by the app, no haggling.

Longtail boats — the heart of getting around Krabi. You need a boat for Railay, the islands, and Khao Khanab Nam. The public boat queue charges per head; you can charter a whole boat but it costs more. Always agree on the fare before you board.
Tour transfers — most island and nature trips include door-to-door transfers from your hotel in the price. Great if you don't want to drive yourself, and they handle timing around the tides for you.

faq.q: What are the must-do Krabi attractions for a first visit?
faq.a: A day on the 4 Islands tour walking the separated sea, Railay Beach with Phra Nang Bay, the Emerald Pool paired with the Hot Spring, and Tiger Cave Temple — that's the set most first-timers in Krabi rarely skip. If you have extra time, add Hong Islands or Phi Phi.

faq.q: How do the 4 Islands tour and Hong Islands differ — which should I pick?
faq.a: The 4 Islands tour is all about Talay Waek and walking the sandbar; it's busier and better for a first visit, with longtail boats around 900–1,200 THB per person. Hong Islands is about the emerald-green inner lagoon and the viewpoint — quieter, with prettier water; longtail boats start around 900 THB and speedboats around 1,100 THB. Both have a national-park fee on top.

faq.q: How much is entry to the Emerald Pool and the Hot Spring, and what are the hours?
faq.a: The Emerald Pool is open roughly 8:30–16:30, with entry around 40 THB for Thais (20 for kids) and around 200 THB for foreigners. The Hot Spring is nearby with entry around 90–200 THB depending on nationality. People love pairing the two in one day since they're on the same route near Khlong Thom. Go in the morning for smaller crowds.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Krabi?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just right for the main sights without rushing. Do one theme per day: the 4 Islands boat tour on day one, the inland nature — hot spring, Emerald Pool, Tiger Cave Temple — on day two, and Railay Beach with the town on day three. If you have more time, add Phi Phi or settle in for a longer stay on Koh Lanta.

faq.q: When's the best time to visit Krabi — can you travel in the rainy season?
faq.a: The clear-water, calm-sea season is November to April, the best time for boat trips out to the islands. In the rainy season (May–Oct) the swell is rough and some tours stop running boats — but the inland nature like the Emerald Pool, the Hot Spring, Tiger Cave Temple, and the town are all fine to visit year-round.
